subject: EU SOC 2 scope, bridge letter and SCCs for cross-border transfers
messages:
From: Emma Laurent <emma.laurent@europayments.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oliver Weber <oliver.weber@europayments.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0400
Subject: SOC 2 Type II and hosting residency questions for EuroPayments PII scope

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Our security team needs to validate Redwood's SOC 2 Type II evidence and clarify hosting/residency controls for our EU card-processing workload. A few specific asks: 

- Can you share your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (audit period + testing dates) and an accompanying bridge letter that covers any gap until your next Type II? KPMG (our assessor) prefers a dated bridge letter signed by your auditor or Redwood legal.
- Please confirm which public cloud regions you operate for the Redwood Hosted product for EU tenants (we need region names and primary replication regions). Is data ever routed or backed up outside the EU for hosted customers?
- What legal mechanisms do you rely on for cross-border transfers (EU SCCs, BCRs, etc.)? If you have a template SCC or a short note on where SCCs are applied (service vs subprocessor), please attach.
- An updated data flow diagram showing data residency (ingest, storage, backups, logs) would be helpful.

Attachments we expect: SOC 2 Type II PDF, bridge letter (PDF), SCC template, data flow diagram. Also please indicate whether Dedicated or Private deployments change the answers above.

Do you have the SOC 2 report and bridge letter available this week? We have an internal deadline end of next week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Laurent
Head of Security, EuroPayments Inc
emma.laurent@europayments.com
+44 20 7946 0123

--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II and hosting residency questions for EuroPayments PII scope

Marissa / Kimberly —

Looping you both in to prepare the SOC2 package and a bridge letter. Key points to confirm in the response: the latest Type II covers 2025 calendar year (Jan 1 2025 - Dec 31 2025) and we can provide a bridge letter dated today confirming no material control changes since the report. For residency: Hosted customers in the EU are assigned to eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) depending on region selection; backups are configured to remain within EU for EU-flagged tenants unless explicitly configured for cross-region DR.

Marissa — can you attach the redacted SOC 2 pdf and draft the bridge letter? Kimberly — can you add a short note re SCCs and DPA (we have standard EU SCCs appended to the DPA) and attach the dataflow diagram.

Emma / Oliver — we can also offer a Private deployment (VPC) if you require contractual EU-only hosting with customer-managed keys.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Laurent <emma.laurent@europayments.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II and hosting residency questions for EuroPayments PII scope

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear ask. Please find the items attached and a short summary below. If you need a KPMG-signed bridge letter we can route through our auditor; otherwise we have an executive-signed bridge letter endorsed by our legal counsel.

Summary (short):
- SOC 2 Type II report: attached (redwood_soc2_typeii_2025.pdf). Audit period tested: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Auditor: Redbridge Audit LLP.
- Bridge letter: attached (redwood_bridge_letter_20260622.pdf). Dated 2026-06-22 and confirms no material control changes impacting scope since the report. We can request auditor signature if you require it — let us know KPMG's preference.
- Hosting / residency: For Redwood Hosted EU tenants we provision in AWS eu-west-1 (primary) and eu-central-1 (secondary/replica). For customers who opt into our EU residency guarantee we configure storage and backups to be restricted to EU regions; logs retention and audit logs are similarly configured for EU-only retention.
- Cross-border transfers: We rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) between Redwood and our customers and with subprocessors as needed. DPA is included in our customer agreements and references SCCs. SCC template attached (redwood_scc_template.pdf).
- Data flow diagram: attached (redwood_eu_dataflow.png) — shows ingestion in eu-west-1, short-lived KV caches, persistent storage in eu-west-1, and monitoring/alerts stored in eu-central-1 replicas for HA. Backups are encrypted and stored in EU-only buckets for EU-flagged tenants.

Notes on Dedicated/Private: Dedicated capacity customers may choose an isolated pool provisioned in EU regions only; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control over network egress and key management. We can provide a short migration checklist if you plan a dedicated/private deployment.

Related links: SOC 2 folder in Drive (shared), DPA and SCC language (HubSpot record) — I included both links in the attachments metadata.

If KPMG needs the bridge letter countersigned by Redbridge Audit LLP, we can engage them; turnaround is typically 5-7 business days.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_soc2_typeii_2025.pdf; redwood_bridge_letter_20260622.pdf; redwood_scc_template.pdf; redwood_eu_dataflow.png

From: Emma Laurent <emma.laurent@europayments.com>

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II and hosting residency questions for EuroPayments PII scope

Marissa — thanks, that helps a lot.

A couple quick follow-ups: 
1) KPMG will confirm whether they need the auditor-signed bridge letter. If they do, please advise next steps and expected timeline (the 5-7 bus. day estimate is fine).
2) For our procurement team: does the DPA + SCCs cover subprocessor transfers to analytics providers (you mentioned subprocessors)? We need the list of subprocessors that may receive telemetry or aggregated logs so we can run a quick vendor review.
3) If we select Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1, please confirm whether replication to eu-central-1 can be disabled entirely (we prefer single-region replication for our compliance profile).

If you can respond to 2 & 3 by early next week that would keep us on track. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emma

On the SOC 2 file: we received the PDF and the bridge letter in your attachments; will route to KPMG today.

--
Emma Laurent
Head of Security, EuroPayments Inc
